title: Inference Gate
homeSummary: A bounded queue for deciding how much inference work to admit.
summary: An inference gateway that compares token-budget admission with a fixed concurrency limit under controlled workloads.
problem: An inference server can accept work faster than it can finish it. Queues grow, deadlines expire, and a fixed request count does not reflect the different sizes of prompts and expected outputs.
approach: Count prompt tokens and reserve capacity for the requested maximum output before admitting work. Bound the queue and reject or expire requests when capacity or time runs out.
Compare token-budget admission with fixed concurrency against the same open-loop request trace. Record outcomes, latency, throughput and peak reservations.
Use a real local Transformers backend for CPU inference, a synthetic fixture for controlled overload, and a vLLM adapter intended for a future free Kaggle GPU run.

decisions.title: Budget for the work, not just the request
decisions.body: Prompt and maximum output tokens determine each reservation. This is a static estimate of memory pressure, not a guarantee against GPU out-of-memory errors.

decisions.title: Hold capacity until work actually ends
decisions.body: A client timeout does not necessarily stop inference. The gateway retains the reservation until the backend finishes; unknown remote outcomes stop new admissions until checked.

decisions.title: Measure useful work alongside latency
decisions.body: Rejecting more requests can lower successful-request latency while reducing completed work. Reports preserve errors and completion counts, not just speed.

limitations: The Kaggle T4/vLLM experiment did not complete: GPU compatibility, memory behavior and performance remain unverified.
One CPU trial is a functional observation, not a statistically supported speedup. The synthetic fixture is not GPU performance evidence.
Local research service: no authentication, distributed admission, streaming or production availability claim. Queued requests are in memory.
M4/MPS execution is implemented but has not been verified on the user's Mac.

diagram.caption: The gateway reserves prompt and maximum output tokens before sending accepted work to an inference engine.

evidence.label: Download source, tests and recorded results

result: Fifteen tests passed locally. One real CPU trial completed 12/12 requests under each policy; one synthetic overload trial showed the token budget capped reservations while rejecting more requests. GPU evaluation remains pending.

title: Durable Tool Runs
homeSummary: Recovering tool runs when an action succeeds but its worker disappears.
summary: A durable execution service for tool-using systems: deduplicated submissions, recoverable workers, and an independently persisted tool provider.
problem: A tool-using system can crash after an external effect commits but before it records success. Retrying blindly can produce a duplicate effect; giving up loses a recoverable run.
approach: Persist sequential steps and an event trail in PostgreSQL. Submission keys deduplicate client retries; renewable leases and fresh claim tokens protect worker ownership.
Call a separate HTTP provider that stores effects in SQLite. Reuse the same tool key after a lost response or worker crash.
Bound retries and request sizes, stop new claims during shutdown, and reconcile uncertain outcomes only after confirming the provider's stored effect.

decisions.title: Separate the effect from the runner
decisions.body: The provider commits outside the runner transaction. A process-kill test exercises the gap between a remote action and locally recorded success.

decisions.title: Protect state and effects separately
decisions.body: Submission keys deduplicate requests, claim tokens fence stale workers, and provider keys protect effects. Each mechanism addresses a different failure boundary.

decisions.title: Keep recovery explicit
decisions.body: Cancellation cannot undo a committed action. Reconciliation verifies the original key and payload before resuming work; missing or conflicting effects stay open for review.

limitations: A single-operator reference service with optional authentication, bounded API behavior and non-root containers. It does not provide tenant isolation, arbitrary tool adapters or automatic compensation.
Retry safety depends on the provider's idempotency contract and retained storage. Unconfirmed effects require operator review.
The free CPU model classified 24/30 held-out synthetic tickets correctly, including errors on two instruction-override cases. All 30 workflows completed; classification still needs human review.
The concurrency and backup checks are bounded local trials, not production capacity or availability guarantees.

diagram.caption: Runner state and provider effects live in separate databases. A reclaimed attempt reuses the provider key; a stale claim cannot overwrite its replacement.

evidence.label: Held-out model predictions and completed runs

result: 45 automated tests passed. In a concurrency check, 100 submissions produced 50 runs and 100 intended effects without duplicates. Backup restoration and desktop/mobile API checks passed. The local model completed all 30 evaluation workflows and classified 24 tickets correctly (macro-F1: 0.803).

title: Agentic Insight Analyst
homeSummary: Tool execution, working memory, and stopping rules.
summary: A feedback-analysis agent with explicit tools, working memory, bounded execution and honest failure reporting.
problem: Turn survey scores and written feedback into a structured report while keeping tool choices and intermediate outputs inspectable.
approach: Inspect a CSV or convert raw feedback into a temporary dataset, then ask a language model to propose analysis steps.
Select from registered tools for TF-IDF clustering, phrase extraction, score analysis, and simple summaries.
Record tool outputs in session memory, evaluate stopping conditions, and synthesize findings and recommendations.

decisions.title: Use a fixed tool registry
decisions.body: The controller validates selected tool names against a registry and prepares arguments in code.

decisions.title: Bound the analysis loop
decisions.body: Iteration limits, repeated-tool detection, and a heuristic progress score determine when analysis stops.

decisions.title: Expose intermediate work
decisions.body: Working memory records plans, tool selections, outputs, and evaluations; the API returns a structured report and execution trace.

limitations: A local, single-process agent prototype; jobs and working memory are not durable across restarts.
Stopping uses a heuristic progress score, not independently verified goal completion.
Offline tests validate execution and failure handling; live report usefulness and factual accuracy remain unmeasured.

diagram.caption: A bounded tool loop turns feedback into a checked report; failed execution is reported explicitly.

result: 35 offline tests cover tools, memory, model and validation failures, raw-text cleanup and job status. Provider errors and unknown tools fail explicitly instead of producing a successful fallback report.

title: Depth Estimation & Segmentation
homeSummary: A TensorNet-based study of shared features for depth and segmentation.
summary: A TensorNet-based PyTorch study of joint foreground segmentation and depth prediction from paired images.
problem: Predict where a foreground object is and its depth using a background image paired with an image containing that object.
approach: Encode the background and composite image separately before combining their representations.
Use residual encoder blocks and skip connections, then decode into separate depth and foreground-mask outputs.
Train with separate scene-disjoint datasets and record normalized-depth RMSE, mask IoU, a checkpoint and input-file hashes.

decisions.title: Learn related tasks together
decisions.body: A shared representation feeds separate decoders for depth and segmentation, while skip connections preserve spatial detail.

decisions.title: Compare the loss functions
decisions.body: The repository documents RMSE, SSIM, binary cross-entropy and Dice experiments rather than presenting one training run as conclusive.

decisions.title: Build on attributed library code
decisions.body: The setup documentation identifies TensorNet v0.9 as the source of the included library code; this case study presents the experiments without claiming a wholly original framework.

limitations: A TensorNet-based paired-image research study; real-data benchmark results have not been independently reproduced.
Inference requires both a background and a composite image.
CPU smoke and training tests use synthetic tensors; they establish runnable training, not depth accuracy.

diagram.caption: A shared encoder representation branches into two task-specific decoders; this schematic condenses the parallel paths.

result: An installable CPU workflow with seven tests covering both output heads, gradients, checkpoint reload, training/validation and overlapping-scene rejection. Historical loss-comparison notebooks retain their original results and attribution.

title: Documentation RAG Pipeline
homeSummary: From documents to retrieved context to generated answers.
summary: A documentation retrieval pipeline with persistent indexing, source-linked answers and explicit abstention.
problem: Answer technical questions using relevant documentation, with separate components for ingestion, retrieval, and generation.
approach: Load web pages and split documents into overlapping chunks.
Embed chunks with OpenAI, persist them in ChromaDB, and retrieve relevant context.
Retrieve once, generate an answer with numbered citations, and return the exact source snippets supplied to the model.

decisions.title: Separate pipeline stages
decisions.body: Document processing, vector storage, and answer generation live in separate classes, making their responsibilities visible.

decisions.title: Keep retrieval configurable
decisions.body: Chunk size and overlap are constructor parameters; retrieval defaults to four matches and accepts search settings.

decisions.title: Check sources and failure paths
decisions.body: Empty retrieval abstains without a model call. Missing or invalid citation IDs and provider failures are rejected; source-labelled cases support retrieval evaluation.

limitations: Citation checks validate source IDs, not whether every statement is supported by the source.
Offline retrieval tests use deterministic embeddings and mocked generation; representative semantic retrieval and answer quality remain unmeasured.
Changed documents create new content-addressed chunks; replacing a corpus requires a fresh collection or database rebuild.

diagram.caption: Retrieved source snippets accompany each answer; empty retrieval abstains and invalid citations fail validation.

result: 10 offline tests exercise chunking, a real persistent Chroma store, duplicate ingestion, citation mapping, abstention and failure propagation. Retrieval metrics run without a paid judge model.

title: Retail Demand Forecasting
summary: A forecasting workbench with leakage-tested features, recursive predictions and a fair comparison against simple baselines.
problem: Compare demand forecasts fairly: the same stores, dates and forecast horizon, using only information available at prediction time.
approach: Validate daily sales and aggregate product rows to a common store/day grain.
Fit naive, seasonal-naive, moving-average and random-forest models before the same temporal cutoff.
Predict the complete held-out horizon recursively, then save aligned predictions and MAE/RMSE results.

decisions.title: Keep simple baselines visible
decisions.body: Naive, seasonal-naive, and moving-average forecasts provide reference approaches alongside tree-based models.

decisions.title: Keep future targets out
decisions.body: Rolling and difference features use prior observations. Recursive forecasts feed predictions back into the next step, never held-out actuals.

decisions.title: Compare like with like
decisions.body: Every model is scored on identical store/date keys. Regression tests change held-out targets and verify that predictions do not change.

limitations: The bundled demonstration is synthetic; its scores are not evidence of performance on real retail demand.
The supported workflow requires complete daily series with at least 60 training days and a shared test horizon.
Historical statistical, boosting and tracking modules remain experimental references outside the maintained core workflow.

diagram.caption: All models forecast the same held-out store/day observations without consuming future targets.

result: 36 offline tests and a complete synthetic demonstration validate the core workflow, including target-leakage regressions and recursive forecasts. Predictions and evaluation metadata are saved for inspection.

title: IntelliQuery: Visual Question Answering
homeSummary: Combining image and question representations to predict an answer.
summary: An image-and-question feature-fusion baseline with image-disjoint evaluation and a training-only answer vocabulary.
problem: Predict an answer to a natural-language question about an image using both visual and textual information.
approach: Load aligned image vectors, question vectors and answer labels from non-object NumPy arrays.
Keep every question about an image in the same partition; fit the answer vocabulary and scaler on training examples only.
Train two 200-unit hidden layers, then report held-out exact match, a majority-answer baseline, vocabulary coverage and per-question predictions.

decisions.title: Split by image, not question
decisions.body: Grouping by image prevents related questions about the same scene from appearing on both sides of the holdout.

decisions.title: Account for unknown answers
decisions.body: Build a vocabulary of up to 500 answers from training data. Test-only answers count as incorrect instead of disappearing from evaluation.

decisions.title: Make the baseline lineage visible
decisions.body: The README links the VQA dataset, related research and upstream demo implementations that informed the experiment.

limitations: The maintained runner is verified on synthetic features; real VQA performance has not been reproduced.
Image and question feature extraction is external to the maintained classifier workflow. Historical BERT/image notebooks remain references.
Lowercase/trim exact match is not the official VQA consensus metric. This is an attributed baseline, not a novel architecture.

diagram.caption: Questions sharing an image stay together; vocabulary and scaling are learned only from training examples.

result: Five offline tests cover image-disjoint splitting, unknown answers, deterministic training, input alignment and rejection of pickle arrays. A small synthetic run exercises training and evaluation without presenting its score as a VQA benchmark.
